sources.entry: CNCjs - Web interface for CNC milling controllers running Grbl, Smoothieware, or TinyG. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: CNCjs is a web-based interface for controlling CNC machines running Grbl, Marlin, Smoothieware, TinyG, or g2core firmware.
summary.what_it_does: CNCjs runs as a Node.js server (installed via npm) and serves a browser-based UI for CNC milling controllers. It supports Grbl, Grbl-Mega, Marlin, Smoothieware, TinyG, and g2core, and can communicate with several clients at once. The interface includes a 6-axis digital readout, 3D tool path visualization, a customizable workspace, and a responsive layout for screens under 720px wide. It also offers a desktop app for Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows, a watch directory for G-code files, custom widgets, custom MDI command buttons, macros, events, keyboard shortcuts, and a Z-probe feature. Pendant and widget add-ons are available through separate projects linked in the README.
use_cases: control a CNC mill from a web browser
run G-code on a Grbl or Marlin machine
monitor CNC jobs over a network
build a Raspberry Pi CNC controller
use a pendant or tablet to jog a CNC machine
how_to_run: Open the web interface in a browser (the README gives the port as 8000 by default)
notable: Supports Grbl, Grbl-Mega, Marlin, Smoothieware, TinyG, and g2core controllers
Plugin ecosystem of custom widgets, pendants, and tablet UIs
Multi-language UI with many translated locales
Desktop app builds for Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows
Optional ~/.cncrc JSON config for mount points, controller, and access settings
caveats: Node.js 14 is the recommended version, per the README's support table
Installing as root requires the --unsafe-perm flag, and installing as a non-root user is advised to avoid serialport issues on some platforms like Raspberry Pi
